decisions.statement: A request is sent to the base handed in at the path that request arrived on.
A caller handing in no base at all has the request sent to Anthropic.
An upstream handed in with one request carries the base and header that request takes.
An upstream handed in is sent with its own header alone and no bearer.
A request is sent with the query that request arrived with.
A request is sent with the method that request arrived with.
A request is sent with the body bytes the caller handed in.
The headers sent upstream are the copy `proxy-headers` makes.
An access token handed in is sent as a bearer `authorization` header.
A request handed no access token has the `authorization` header the client sent.
A request with no authorization of either sort is sent with no authorization header.
An idle guard is armed on `/v1/messages`.
An idle guard is armed on `/v1/messages/count_tokens`.
A path neither messages API answers is sent unguarded.
An idle span at zero or below leaves a request unguarded.
An observer is built where a log file is handed in.
An observer is built where the slot has an end.
A slot with no end beside no log file is left with nothing.
An observer that is built is put in the slot the caller handed in.
An observer already in the slot is ended before the new observer lands.
A replaced observer is ended as a client disconnect.
The upstream status reaches the observer.
The observer's start is stamped before the upstream fetch opens.
A response the upstream gives no body for ends its observer at once.
A keepalive is armed only where the upstream content type has the SSE type.
A keepalive is armed only where the downstream keepalive span is above zero.
An SSE error frame is served only where the upstream content type has that type.
The response has the upstream status.
The response has the upstream status text.
The response headers are the copy `proxy-headers` makes.
The file a transport row lands beside is handed in rather than a directory.
The clock is handed in so a test needs no real time.
The timers are handed in so a test needs no wait.
The fetch is handed in so a test needs no network.
A caller hands the whole request body in as one buffer.
A caller hands one slot to every attempt one client request is served by.
A caller arms the end on the observer left in the slot.
A caller hands in the path of a page file a transport row lands beside.
Nothing here reads the index.
Nothing here resolves a page.
Nothing here writes a transport row.
Nothing here retries a request.
Nothing here chooses the account a request is sent under.
Nothing here has a clock the caller cannot replace.
An upstream fetch that throws before a response arrives reaches no observer.
A fetch that throws leaves the slot with the observer of the attempt before.
Anthropic's own base is written here as the base a caller may leave unsaid.
The two guarded paths are written here rather than handed in.
A keepalive emitter is armed on the real timers.
The observer's start covers the upstream connect as well as the stream.
An observer is left in the slot after the response is handed back.
A request body reaching upstream is a whole buffer rather than a stream.

definition: one client request sent on to a provider and the response streamed back
